value.rationale: For r>=3, direct counting at N_a(X)^r≈(log X)^2 yields only O(X) and cannot establish density zero. The theorem proves genuine sparsity precisely on this borderline for every fixed r, exhibited by the explicit chain k!2^{ceil(k^{r/2})}. It extends a motivated necessary-condition question beyond two shifts and classifies a natural general quadratic-form local obstruction. This is a mathematical theorem, not merely another numerical case or a substitution of coefficients; the exponent is sufficient, not claimed optimal.
